govdocs-archive_org-noob-flushyourmeds_N:
Scott A. Barry's NOOB #flushyourmeds is an e-book that mixes two subjects few books combine: beginner occult instruction and practical notes on digital privacy. Its title addresses the reader as a noob, a newcomer to both crafts at once.

Alongside occult material and numerology, Barry writes about MAC spoofing and routing traffic through Tor, the tools of staying anonymous online. The text is fragmentary and eclectic, jumping between its worlds without apology. The result is a strange hybrid from the internet's occult underground, where magic and operational security are treated as one art.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-AllenMarkFOIASe:
When the House Select Committee on Assassinations took up the murders of John F. Kennedy and Martin Luther King Jr. in the late 1970s, its members and staff needed a common base of background information. This briefing book was prepared for the committee to supply it.

The volume gathers the background the reinvestigation worked from, and it survives here as researcher Mark Allen's FOIA selection, drawn from disclosures dated April 12, 1984. Briefing books show what investigators were told before they began asking questions, which makes them evidence in their own right. The file is a public record of the second official inquiry.
podcast-dannyjones-y3XbBfTqcSc:
Wildlife host Forrest Galante joins Danny Jones to talk about DNA scientists who plan to build a real Jurassic Park by 2027. Galante is a biologist known for hunts for lost species. The plan at issue is de-extinction, the bid to bring back the dead.

Galante walks through the labs that aim to revive lost beasts from old DNA. He weighs which beasts could walk again first and what parks might hold them. Jones asks where the plan could go wrong. Listeners get a wild but real tale from the edge of gene work. The library files the talk as an archive record.
podcast-tuckercarlson-DG-dcjlzCsc:
Tucker Carlson declares that the ruling class is losing control. His short title carries the whole thesis of the hour. He points to cracks in media, courts, and party power.

Carlson argues that elite panic shows in bans, suits, and harsh words. Each move, he says, admits that old tools fail. He urges viewers to read fear as a sign of change. The episode is a rallying brief for the hopeful and the rebellious. It gives no guest and no hedge: one host reads the moment as a turning of the tide.
doe-osti-3399495-collaborative-research-: Magnetic reconnection — field lines snapping and rejoining — powers solar flares and auroras. This collaborative research builds interpretable data-driven models that work across scales, from lab plasmas to space. Understandable AI for one of physics' most violent processes.
doe-osti-3484786-toward-next-generation-: Science runs on software — but the tools are scattered across fields. This report charts next-generation ecosystems for scientific computing, pulling together community, software, and AI so teams from different fields can build as one. The vision is a shared toolkit for physicists, biologists, and engineers alike.
